Expected results

  • The Invoiced and Paid cards and rows carry a lock icon, the visible sign that they can only be reordered within their current technician and not moved to another one.
  • Hovering the lock icon shows the tooltip “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-1] and “Paid · can’t be reassigned” on [WO-2].
  • Reassign lead technician and Unassign are shown disabled, and their tooltip reads exactly: Invoiced · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-1]) or Paid · can’t be reassigned (on [WO-2]). (A straight or curly apostrophe is not a difference.)
  • While [WO-1] or [WO-2] is dragged over [Tech-B]'s column or group, the note at its top reads “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-1]) or “Paid · can’t be reassigned” (for [WO-2]).
  • On release the drop is refused: the card or row stays with [Tech-A], and its lead stays [Tech-A].

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-N6, S4-N7 and S4-N2, read 19 Oct 2026. PRD §9 User Feedback Summary row "Reassignment not allowed in current status". Design export of 8 Oct 2026 (Claude Design project 787fef1a, Work Orders.dc.html): lock icon next to the number with tooltip "Invoiced · can’t be reassigned" and a locked menu note; since PRD version 68 the PRD uses the same words, and the PRD text is asserted here. Source-verified 19 October 2026.

PRD version 82 (29 Oct 2026, SV-11902; read 29 Oct 2026): a Declined work order now locks its lead technician exactly like an Invoiced or Paid one; the quotes below are from version 82. What this case checks is unchanged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-N6: “On a Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order the Assign lead technician or Reassign lead technician action (S3-R14) and the Unassign action are disabled, and their tooltip reads “Declined · can’t be reassigned”, “Invoiced · can’t be reassigned” or “Paid · can’t be reassigned”, in the design’s format. The same words are the tooltip on the card’s or row’s lock icon, and the note shown at the top of another technician’s column or group while the work order is dragged over it, where the drop is refused.”
  • S4-N7: “Visually indicate that a Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order can only be reordered within its current technician, not moved to another one.”
  • S4-N2: “Do not allow the lead technician to change in Declined, Invoiced or Paid status. A Declined, Invoiced or Paid work order can still be dragged to reorder it within its current technician (or within Unassigned), but it cannot be moved to another technician, to Unassigned, or out of Unassigned. Complete work orders can be moved freely, as today. The lock follows the work order’s status at the moment of the change: a work order is Declined only while every one of its lines is declined, so when a line is re-approved or a new line is added and the work order becomes Estimate or Approved, its lead can change again. Only the work order’s own status counts: a declined line on a work order in any other status does not lock it.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.
